sections.content:
11,910 people

were counted on the census as "horticultural trades" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Horticultural trades workers intensively cultivate vegetables, plants, fruit, shrubs, trees and flowers in greenhouses, market gardens, nurseries and orchards.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "horticultural trades" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "horticultural trades", 12.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "horticultural trades" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "horticultural trades" included:

  • telephonists
  • receptionists
  • market research interviewers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "horticultural trades" there were a similar number of men and women (52.5% compared with 47.5%).

This means "horticultural trades" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled agricultural and related trades".

Men made up 52.5% and women made up 47.5% of "horticultural trades"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "horticultural trades" included:

  • higher education teaching professionals
  • taxation experts
  • debt, rent and other cash collectors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "horticultural trades" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "horticultural trades" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "horticultural trades", 11.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (69% compared with 31%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (70.4%) than self-employed (29.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
